findings.title: Cross-adapter multipart test is a stale reflection stopgap that bypasses the real request accessors
findings.description: The class comment still says the handler reaches the parser 'the way the request accessors of a later fragment will', and upload() calls DefaultRequest.bodyStream via setAccessible(true), then runs MultipartParser.parse directly with its own MultipartSettings, a literal 1048576L form limit and a fresh SpoolRegistry. The accessors now exist (req.file/parts/form), so this test never exercises DefaultRequest.formData, BodyState.sharedParse, the app spool registry, onError or the standard 413/400 error body over TinyHttpd. FR-MULTIPART-001 AC-1 requires the T13-T16 tests to run over both adapters with the same results; the TinyHttpd side here only tests the parser over a socket stream, not the framework path.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the reflection helper; register a handler that calls req.parts()/req.file() on an app configured with app.multipart(o -> o.tempDirectory(tmp)), and assert status plus standard error body for the 400/413 cases on both adapters.

findings.title: FR-MULTIPART-004 AC-5 (text-part total capped by formLimit) and AC-2 (heap bound) have no test
findings.description: MultipartParser caps text parts with formLimit - textTotal, but no test sends one text part of 1048576 bytes (accepted), one of 1048577 (413) or two of 600000 (413), and none checks the 413 standard error body for it; grep for 600000/1048577/'FR-MULTIPART-004 AC-5' finds nothing in the multipart tests. The heap-bound AC (32 MiB upload, < 8 MiB heap growth with the default threshold) has no test either; MultipartSpoolingTest covers only AC-1/AC-3/AC-4. A regression that dropped the text total or buffered spooled parts in memory would pass the suite.
findings.suggested_fix: Add MultipartLimitsTest cases for the three AC-5 sizes through req.form() with an end-to-end 413 body check; add a heap test (System.gc + MemoryMXBean used-heap delta while the handler holds a 32 MiB UploadFile).

findings.title: Multipart 400/413 limits are only tested against the parser, not through the accessor and onError
findings.description: parse()/assert413 call MultipartParser.parse directly and only check HttpException.status(). FR-MULTIPART-002 AC-1 and FR-MULTIPART-001 AC-2/AC-4 require each 413/400 to carry the FR-APP-006 standard error body and pass through onError when an accessor reads the body. Nothing checks that path end to end for maxFileSize, maxParts, maxRequestSize, header limits or a bad boundary.
findings.suggested_fix: Add at least one app-level test per limit kind asserting status, standard error body and that an onError handler saw the HttpException.

findings.title: Quoted-string backslash unescaping mangles real browser filenames
findings.description: params() treats a backslash inside a quoted value as an escape and drops it. Browsers do not escape backslashes in the Content-Disposition filename (the HTML multipart encoding only percent-encodes '"', CR and LF), and some clients send 'C:\fakepath\a.txt'; filename() then returns 'C:fakepatha.txt', violating FR-MULTIPART-004 AC-4 (filename unchanged). MultipartSpoolingTest line 90 hides this by doubling the backslash on the wire before sending.
findings.suggested_fix: For Content-Disposition parameters keep backslashes literally (end the quoted value only at '"'), or unescape only an escaped quote and an escaped backslash; change the test to send the raw single backslash as a browser does.

findings.title: Uploads are released when the response completes, so save() after res.send() in the same handler throws
findings.description: releaseUploads() runs in res.onDone, which fires as soon as a non-streaming response is delivered, while the handler may still be running. A handler doing res.status(202).send("queued"); f.save(dest); gets IllegalStateException 'used after its request ended'. docs/api/multipart.md:123 tells users to save() inside the handler, which does not hold once the response was sent; respond-then-process is common for Express/multer users.
findings.suggested_fix: Release when both the response is done and the handler returned (Dispatcher finish/after-handler path), or document that the request ends at response completion and add a save-after-send test.

findings.title: res.download leaves Content-Disposition set when the file lookup fails after it was added
findings.description: answerFile puts Content-Disposition: attachment before FileResponder.respond, which can still throw FileNotFoundException/IOException (r.length, r.open). The default error path clears headers in afterFailure, but a user onError handler that writes res.status(404).json(...) keeps the attachment header, so the browser downloads the error JSON as a file.
findings.suggested_fix: Add Content-Disposition only after the resolver checks pass (pass it into FileResponder to set at commit), or remove it in the catch blocks.

findings.title: Telescoping Dispatcher/DefaultRequest constructors create orphan SpoolRegistry instances no shutdown participant closes
findings.description: Three extra Dispatcher overloads and the 7-arg DefaultRequest constructor (DefaultRequest.java:79-80) build new MultipartSettings()/new SpoolRegistry() defaults. Temp files created through these paths are outside the app spool and are never deleted by the AFTER_ON_STOP participant (FR-MULTIPART-006 AC-2). They exist only to keep older tests compiling, and each wave adds another overload.
findings.suggested_fix: Collapse to one constructor taking the full config (or a small settings holder) and update the tests, so no code path can spool outside the app registry.

findings.title: Default formLimit 1048576L is a magic literal duplicated in three classes
findings.description: 1048576L appears in DefaultRestApp.java:103, Dispatcher.java:99 and DefaultRequest.java:79 (plus tests), while jsonLimit uses JsonBodyReader.DEFAULT_LIMIT. Changing the default in one place silently diverges the others.
findings.suggested_fix: Add FormBodyReader.DEFAULT_LIMIT and reference it everywhere.

findings.title: MultipartOptions javadoc says 'no value means unlimited', which reads as the opposite of the contract
findings.description: '...and no value means unlimited' reads as 'leaving a setting unset means unlimited', but unset means the listed defaults and unlimited is impossible (IR-MULTIPART-001 AC-3).
findings.suggested_fix: Reword: 'no setting accepts an unlimited value; an unset setting keeps its default'.

findings.title: DefaultUploadFile keeps every stream it ever handed out until request end
findings.description: inputStream() appends to streams and nothing removes a stream when the caller closes it; FormData.utf8, bytes() and transferTo() each add one. A handler that calls bytes() repeatedly grows the list and keeps FileInputStream objects reachable for the whole request.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the stream from the list in ClosableStream.close() (callback to the owner), or keep only open streams.

findings.title: Disconnect test uses a same-thread CountDownLatch as a boolean and sleep-polling
findings.description: 'spooled' is counted down and awaited with 0 s on the test thread, so it is just a boolean, and two 5 ms sleep loops make the test timing-dependent: on a slow CI the spool may appear after the 5 s poll and the test fails spuriously.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a plain assert for the spool check and a latch the server side counts down once the temp file exists; keep one bounded poll for the directory.
